Q: Why can't I use Iterable as a type for overloading a singledispatchmethod? A:

the reason is 2 thing:

1)typing.Iterable is defined as _alias(collections.abc.Iterable, 1) which is a instance of some custom class on that module, that happens to work with isinstance

2)functools.singledispatchmethod in its implementation do the following test isinstance(arg, type) along the way, for which isinstance(typing.Iterable, type) == False fails by virtue of being an instance of a class

Solution: use collections.abc.Iterable instead of typing.Iterable, because is an actual class.

That is the same reason why numbers.Number also works too, is also an actual class rather than this weird alias thing on the typing module, both also predate that module too.

And for if it is a bug, probably yeah, they hadn't go and make functools, or single dispach in any case compatible with the typing module, unless that happens to be intentional. But I can't tell you which with certainty.
